text.p: Bangladesh Home Minister Rafiqul Islam said on Friday that police had arrested 1,110 "terrorists" since Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina took office four months ago.
More than 2,000 weapons of different kinds have been seized while unauthorised holders handed in 715 more, the minister told parliament.
Police estimated in August that nearly 100,000 firearms and a huge quantity of explosives were in illegal hands, for use in a wide range of crimes from robbery to political killings.
The main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party has said more than 100 of its workers and supporters have been killed since the election of the current parliament in June.
The new parliament began its second session on Friday.

It has sensitive issues on its business agenda, including law and order and the repeal of an ordinance protecting the alleged killers of Bangladesh's independence leader, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, parliament officials said.
Mujib, Hasina's father, was killed in a 1975 army coup with most of his family.
